headline: Volkswagen Recalls 49,958 MY2025 Tiguans for BCM Software Fault That Can Stall Engine Mid-Drive
gist: NHTSA campaign 26V587 (filed ~25 Sep 2026) covers 49,958 MY2025 Tiguan SUVs whose Body Control Module software mishandles ECC errors, causing unexpected BCM resets that can switch off the ignition, disable exterior lighting, airbags and rearview camera while driving. Dealers will reflash BCM software to version 0326 or newer at no charge; owner notification letters are expected 6 November 2026.

headline: Rivian Recalls ~100,700 Vehicles Over Software Prompt That Can Block Rearview Camera Display
gist: Rivian filed a recall on 23 September 2026 covering 2022-2026 R1T, 2022-2027 R1S and 2027 R2 models because a stability-control re-enable prompt can obscure the rearview camera image in reverse, breaching FMVSS 111. More than 95% of affected vehicles already carried the OTA fix at time of filing, making this effectively an administrative compliance action.

headline: Ford Rearview Camera Recall (26C42) Added to NHTSA Database; Owner Letters Due 5 October 2026
gist: NHTSA campaign 26V605000/26C42 for Ford Motor Company, covering 11,405 vehicles for a rearview camera image display non-compliance (FMVSS 111), had VINs searchable from 25 September 2026. Interim owner notification letters are scheduled to be mailed 5 October 2026 while the remedy remains under development.

headline: NHTSA Batch Recall Round-Up: Ford, GM, VW, Hyundai, Chrysler — Software and Airbag Defects Dominate Late-September 2026
gist: A new batch of NHTSA safety recall notices published around 21 September 2026 covers multiple OEMs including VW Tiguan BCM software (26V587), VW/Audi bolt failure (26V590), Ford airbag deployment (26V581/26V580), and Ford BECM software causing loss of power or fire risk (26V582). Software glitches and airbag concerns are listed alongside mechanical issues, reflecting the growing dominance of electronic defect categories.

headline: EU Data Act One-Year Balance: Major OEM API Infrastructure Now Live, Fleet Telematics Data Access 'Almost a Commodity'
gist: A September 2026 analysis by Optivo Logistics finds that between October 2025 and March 2026 all major automotive groups completed API infrastructure to expose telematics data to third-party providers under Regulation (EU) 2023/2854. Fleet managers can now nominate telematics platforms to receive live vehicle data without OEM-imposed contracts, though adoption remains uneven across EU member states.

headline: Jeep Grand Cherokee/Wagoneer TPMS Software Recall: 201,976 Vehicles, 100% Defect Rate
gist: NHTSA recall 26V559 (dated 1 September 2026) covers 201,976 Jeep Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer family vehicles from model years 2024-2026 whose Radio Frequency Hub module software causes the tire pressure monitoring system to lose reference pressures and fail to warn drivers. FCA US estimates 100% of vehicles in the production window carry the defect.

headline: Renault Trafic e-Tech to Launch on Android Automotive OS SDV Platform in Late 2026, Validating AAOS for Commercial Vehicles
gist: Google's Android Automotive OS developer blog confirmed that Renault is leveraging the AAOS SDV platform — featuring modular structure, topology-agnostic communication, and granular OTA update support — for its upcoming Renault Trafic e-Tech commercial vehicle, with production set to begin in late 2026. Google is concurrently preparing an open-source release of the AAOS SDV platform for broader ecosystem partners.

headline: EU Data Act Vehicle Data Sharing: Transconnect Analysis Highlights Remaining Lock-In Gaps for Dealers and Fleet Owners
gist: A late-September 2026 Transconnect analysis notes that while Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 gives fleet owners the right to nominate third-party telematics recipients, the scope is limited to raw and pre-processed data and excludes derived algorithmic insights — leaving significant proprietary data still under OEM control. Uneven EU member-state adoption and unanswered questions over inferred data remain key friction points for fleet operators.

headline: Ransomware Attacks on Auto Industry More Than Doubled in 2025; JLR Global Production Halted Three Weeks by Attack
gist: A CBT News investigation (published mid-2026) reports that ransomware incidents in the automotive sector more than doubled in 2025, reaching 44% of all cyber incidents in the industry, with attackers increasingly targeting connected vehicles directly via cloned SIMs and expired virtual numbers. A ransomware attack halted all Jaguar Land Rover global production for over three weeks in October 2025, causing an estimated $2.5 billion in economic damage.

headline: Upstream Security: EU's 2026 Mandate Requires Live Digital Twins and AI Behavioral Monitoring for Connected Vehicle Security
gist: Upstream Security's analysis of the EU's 2026 connected-vehicle security mandate argues that 'factory-gate' security is no longer sufficient against organized nation-state actors, and that OEMs now need live digital twins per vehicle to establish telematics baselines and flag anomalies in real time. The platform uses agentic AI to correlate data from the vehicle, supply chain, and cloud to meet the new EU situational-awareness requirements.

headline: Viasat & 5GAA Survey: NTN Satellite Connectivity Represents Commercial Inflection Point for Automotive OEMs
gist: A Viasat/5GAA report (published ~August 2026) based on a 1,606-driver survey across 10 markets finds that Direct-to-Device (D2D) NTN, enabled by 3GPP Release 17, allows a single automotive SIM to connect to both terrestrial and satellite networks simultaneously for the first time. OEMs are assessed as being at a commercial inflection point where NTN can extend connected-car services beyond cellular gaps and unlock new tiering and upselling models.

headline: Berg Insight: 583 Million Connected Cars by 2030 on Back of SGP.32 eSIM, 5G RedCap and Satellite — G+D, Rivian, AT&T Ink SGP.32 Deal
gist: Berg Insight's July 2026 flagship report forecasts the global active installed base of OEM-embedded telematics vehicles will reach 583.1 million by 2030 at an 11.5% CAGR, with 83% of 2025 new cars already shipping with embedded connectivity. The next-growth layer is expected to rely on the new SGP.32 eSIM standard and early satellite integration; G+D, Rivian and AT&T announced a collaboration to build SGP.32-compliant eSIM connectivity into Rivian's R2 platform.

headline: UNECE R155 & R156 Enforcement Spotlight: 2027 Compliance Deadline Drives OEM CSMS Audits and SBOM Obligations
gist: A late-September 2026 Automotive IQ explainer confirms that UN R155 (paired with ISO/SAE 21434) mandates a certified Cyber Security Management System across the vehicle lifecycle, with the EU Cyber Resilience Act adding explicit SBOM requirements expected from 2027. Technical services are actively auditing OEM CSMS implementations per ISO 21434 on behalf of type-approval authorities across 60+ UNECE contracting parties.

headline: Webfleet 2026 Fleet Trends: EU LCV Tachograph Rule Extension from July 2026 Accelerates Digital Telematics Adoption
gist: Webfleet's 2026 fleet-trends forecast notes that from July 2026 EU driving and rest-time rules extended to light commercial vehicles over 2.5 tonnes in cross-border traffic, significantly expanding the mandatory digital tachograph compliance market beyond traditional heavy-truck fleets. The telematics provider positions AI-powered analytics for route planning, regulatory compliance, cost analysis, and vehicle condition forecasting as the primary response to these converging cost and regulatory pressures.

headline: SDV Summit 2026 (Pune, 8-9 Oct): Industry Convenes on Vehicle OS, OTA, Zonal Architecture and Cybersecurity
gist: The SDV Summit 2026, scheduled for 8-9 October 2026 in Pune, India, brings together automotive leaders and embedded-systems engineers to address OTA updates, AI-driven vehicle architectures, zonal compute, cybersecurity and connected mobility — reflecting the sector's shift from exploratory SDV projects to production deployment. The event falls within the target scan window and signals growing Asia-Pacific industry alignment on SDV standards.

headline: NHTSA Issues Special Order to Tesla on Cybercab FMVSS Self-Certification; Response Deadline September 30
gist: NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ26002 on September 4, 2026, covering ~1,000 Cybercabs deployed in Austin, and on September 10 issued a formal Special Order demanding sworn answers to 21 questions about how Tesla self-certified the no-steering-wheel, no-pedal robotaxi as FMVSS-compliant. Tesla's response was due September 30, 2026, the day falling within the scan window.

headline: China CSRC Applies Three-Criteria 'Window Guidance' to Cool Humanoid-Robot IPO Pipeline
gist: China's securities regulator informally told humanoid-robot IPO applicants they must demonstrate sustainable revenue and commercial orders, narrowing losses (with a three-year forecast), and ownership of core technology such as robotic brains or hands. The guidance, reported September 29, 2026, comes after Unitree Robotics' Shanghai debut saw shares surge nearly 500% then retreat sharply, and with at least two dozen embodied-AI companies having filed to list in Hong Kong alone.

headline: IDC: China Accounts for 77.9% of Global Humanoid Robot Shipments in H1 2026; Forecast Raised to 750,000 Units by 2030
gist: IDC data published September 29, 2026 shows China shipped more than 19,000 humanoid robots in the first half of 2026, representing 77.9% of nearly 25,000 global shipments—a 432% year-on-year jump. IDC simultaneously raised its 2030 global humanoid-robot shipment forecast to more than 750,000 units.

headline: FCC Adds Foreign-Produced Humanoid Robots and Quadrupeds to Covered List, Blocking New Equipment Authorizations
gist: On July 28, 2026 the FCC's Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau enacted Public Notice DA 26-786, adding foreign-produced advanced robotic devices—explicitly including autonomous mobile robots, humanoids, and quadrupeds over 4.4 lb with network connectivity—to the Covered List, following a White House-convened interagency National Security Determination citing cybersecurity vulnerabilities (including remote takeover risk) and supply-chain risks. New foreign-built robot models cannot receive FCC equipment authorization without DoW Conditional Approval; previously authorized devices remain grandfathered through at least 2029.

headline: Zoox Granted First-Ever NHTSA Commercial Exemption for Purpose-Built Robotaxi; NHTSA Signals FMVSS Update
gist: NHTSA granted Zoox a temporary commercial exemption allowing up to 2,500 purpose-built robotaxi vehicles annually for two years—the first such exemption for a driverless vehicle lacking conventional controls—announced alongside NHTSA's July 30, 2026 AV fast-track package. NHTSA also stated intent to update FMVSS and is developing National Competency Standards (behavioral competency test protocols) for ADS-equipped vehicles.
outlet: Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety / NHTSA (saferoads.org citing NHTSA)

headline: Tesla Cybercab Begins Paid Commercial Rides in Austin; NHTSA FSD Probe Covers 3.2 Million Vehicles Simultaneously
gist: Tesla's Cybercab—designed with no steering wheel, pedals, mirrors, or rear window and using a camera-only autonomy stack—started offering paid public rides in Austin on September 3, 2026, with over one million unsupervised miles accumulated by the fleet as of that month. NHTSA simultaneously maintains a separate probe into Full Self-Driving software across approximately 3.2 million Tesla vehicles.

headline: Agility Robotics Explores Wheeled Robot Form Factors Beyond Digit Humanoid to Broaden Industrial Deployments
gist: Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit humanoid, confirmed on September 25, 2026 it is exploring wheeled and other non-humanoid robot designs to address operating environments where bipedal form factors are less practical, signaling a platform diversification strategy as humanoids move from demo to industrial deployment. The move reflects industry-wide pressure to prove commercial viability beyond warehouse pilots.

headline: Waabi–Uber Partnership to Deploy 25,000 AI-Driven Robotaxis on Uber Platform Progresses in 2026
gist: Waabi, which launched a partnership with Uber in January 2026 to deploy 25,000 robotaxis on Uber's platform, continues scaling its end-to-end generative-AI autonomous driving system. The company's Waabi Driver is integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous Truck (launched October 2025), creating a dual commercial-vehicle and robotaxi AI licensing model.

headline: Japan Active Cyber Defense Law Enacted; Enters Force October 2026 with Implications for Connected-Vehicle and Robot OT Security
gist: Japan's revised Active Cyber Defense law, passed August 28, 2026 by the National Diet and effective October 1, 2026, extends government authority to proactively neutralize threats in OT networks including those supporting connected vehicles and industrial robots, granting limited countermeasure powers to police and the Self-Defense Forces. The law was flagged by Japanese security analysts as relevant to automotive OEMs and robot OEMs operating industrial control systems subject to UN-R155.

headline: UN-R155 / EU CRA Driving Automotive Cybersecurity Market Toward Robots and Physical-AI Platforms — VicOne Japan Analysis
gist: VicOne Japan's representative detailed in trade press how UN-R155 (CSMS) and UN-R156 (SUMS) created the automotive cybersecurity market by tying type approval to security management obligations, and argued the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)—covering all networked products—will replicate that dynamic for humanoid robots and drones. The analysis highlights AI-assisted threat and risk assessment (TARA) acceleration as the next compliance frontier for physical-AI OEMs.

headline: NHTSA AV First-Responder Remediation Deadline Passes; No Operator Submission Made Public
gist: NHTSA's July 31, 2026 deadline for AV operators to submit first-responder interaction remediation plans has passed as of the scan window, but the agency has made no operator's submission public and announced no enforcement outcome. The NHTSA administrator had previously described AVs that cannot safely interact with first responders as 'a danger to the general public' and threatened enforcement action.
outlet: The Charge Port / Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety

headline: Lytx Launches LytxOne: Unified Video Telematics, Safety, and Fleet Maintenance Platform for Commercial Fleets
gist: Lytx announced LytxOne, a unified fleet management platform combining video safety, telematics, and maintenance into a single system, targeting commercial fleets including those operating autonomous and semi-autonomous vehicles. The launch reflects continued industry consolidation of fragmented telematics stacks into integrated AI-powered platforms with remote diagnostics and driver-behavior scoring.

headline: Mobilisights Rebrands as Mobilisights Connect, Expanding Stellantis B2B Connected-Vehicle Data and Fleet Telematics Offer
gist: Stellantis rebranded its connected-vehicle data division as Mobilisights Connect and expanded its B2B software offering for fleet managers, providing APIs and software solutions tied directly to factory-embedded OEM telematics. The move intensifies competition with aftermarket TSPs as OEM-embedded data feeds become the industry baseline for fleet remote diagnostics and usage analytics.

headline: China Defence Mobilisation Law (Revised) Takes Effect October 1, 2026: Data and Cyber Assets of Private Firms Subject to Requisition
gist: China's revised National Defence Mobilisation Law, passed August 28 and effective October 1, 2026, extends requisition authority to private-sector data assets and cyber resources, raising compliance and data-sovereignty concerns for international robotics OEMs and AV operators with operations or joint ventures in China. The law's broad scope over 'data and cyber' resources is flagged as material for connected-vehicle and industrial-robot supply chains.

headline: ISO 10218 Revised Collaborative-Robot Safety Standard Now Reflected in Japan JIS B 8433; ISO/TS 15066 Upgrade to Full IS Under Discussion
actors: Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
gist: Japan is incorporating the 2024 revision of ISO 10218 (industrial robot safety, with expanded collaborative-operation requirements) into the national JIS B 8433 standard, as Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare simultaneously reviews updating the industrial-safety regulation (Aneisei) to reflect modern cobot technology. ISO/TS 15066 (cobot contact-force limits) is under discussion for elevation to a full ISO International Standard, with new contact-force thresholds and safety-evaluation methods being debated.

headline: General Motors Launches OnStar Fleet Intelligence Platform
gist: On 30 September 2026, GM unveiled the OnStar Fleet Intelligence platform, a centralised service integrating vehicle data with connected services to optimise asset utilisation, risk management and operating expenses for fleet managers. The launch marks a strategic move to leverage telematics and connected vehicle data for commercial fleet customers.

headline: Motum Receives Frost & Sullivan 2026 Mexican Connected Truck Telematics Innovation Leadership Award
gist: On 30 September 2026, Frost & Sullivan awarded Motum its 2026 Transformational Innovation Leadership Recognition in the Mexican connected truck telematics industry for achievements in AI-powered driver monitoring, intelligent engine immobilisation, and cargo-theft prevention. Units protected by Motum technology reportedly register ten times fewer thefts than the national industry average.

headline: Telematics Systems Market 2026–2034 Report Published, Forecasting 11.5% CAGR Driven by AI Fleet Management
gist: Published on 30 September 2026, the report forecasts the telematics systems market will grow at an 11.5% CAGR through 2034, with demand driven by route optimisation, predictive maintenance, AI-powered fleet analytics, and connected-car expansion. The report covers recurring revenue models, emerging markets and investment activity.

headline: Iridium & Deutsche Telekom IoT Complete Global Roaming Agreement; Toyota Vehicle Sends First NB-IoT Satellite Voice Message
gist: On 10 September 2026, Iridium and Deutsche Telekom IoT demonstrated a standards-based NB-IoT voice message sent from a Toyota vehicle over Iridium NTN Direct LEO satellites, completing a global roaming agreement. Commercial availability for DT IoT customers targeting automotive, logistics and fleet use cases is planned for Q4 2026.

headline: Thales, Singtel, Optus, AIS and Globe Telecom Deploy Multi-Network IoT eSIM Platform Using GSMA SGP.32
gist: Thales and four mobile operators deployed a multi-operator IoT eSIM network based on GSMA SGP.32, enabling connected vehicles and fleet devices to switch between participating networks across borders without SIM replacement. The rollout extends seamless eSIM management to the automotive and commercial-fleet segment across Asia-Pacific.

headline: Soracom Launches Automotive Suite API Platform for Connected-Vehicle Lifecycle Management with SGP.32 eSIM
gist: Soracom launched its Automotive Suite, an API-driven platform combining SGP.32 eSIM profile switching, multi-carrier management, in-car Wi-Fi, usage-based billing and support for European eCall services. The platform is designed to manage connected-vehicle connectivity throughout the vehicle lifecycle.

headline: Motorq and Toyota North America to Present on Embedded OEM Telematics for Mixed Fleets
gist: Motorq and Toyota North America announced a session to discuss using factory-embedded vehicle data alongside aftermarket devices to unify mixed-fleet telematics and reduce costs. The initiative targets fleet operators managing vehicles from multiple OEMs with heterogeneous data streams.

headline: Vicovanu Transport Expands KRONE Telematics Rollout to 70 Connected Trailers for Live Tracking and Diagnostics
gist: UK container operator Vicovanu Transport ordered 15 additional KRONE Box Liner trailers and extended KRONE Telematics to 70 units, enabling live tracking, remote diagnostics, maintenance planning and tyre monitoring across the fleet. The rollout reflects growing adoption of factory-embedded trailer telematics in logistics fleets.

headline: Romania TollRo Road-Charge Scheme Commences 1 October 2026 for Commercial Vehicles Over 3.5t
gist: Romania's TollRo electronic road-charge scheme for HGVs over 3.5 tonnes launched on 1 October 2026, requiring operators to choose between route tickets, the eTarife app or OBU-based SETRo contracts. The mandate creates new in-cab OBU and telematics compliance requirements for cross-border commercial fleets.

headline: Fleet Data Silos Hinder AI Integration and Technology Adoption Across Commercial Fleets, FleetOwner Analysis Finds
gist: FleetOwner published analysis showing that fragmented telematics, maintenance and operational data silos are limiting fleet efficiency and AI integration, with surveys revealing low levels of full technology adoption. Vendors are responding by developing unified workflows, natural-language tools and edge-processing capabilities.

headline: British Columbia Passes Commercial Dash Camera Mandate for Fleet Vehicles
gist: The province of British Columbia enacted a mandate requiring dash cameras on commercial fleet vehicles, making it one of the first North American jurisdictions to legislate forward-facing video recording for commercial transport. The rule is expected to drive telematics and AI-camera adoption across BC-registered commercial fleets.

headline: Panasonic Group Launches VERZEUSE for TARA, ISO/SAE 21434-Compliant Threat Analysis Solution for SDV Era
gist: Panasonic Group announced free trial availability of VERZEUSE for TARA, an ISO/SAE 21434-compliant threat-analysis-and-risk-assessment solution designed for complex SDV architectures as well as simpler ECU configurations. The tool is aimed at helping OEMs and suppliers meet UN R155 CSMS requirements across vehicle programmes.
outlet: Nikkei / PR TIMES (company newsroom via trade press)

headline: Mlink Begins Live On-Air Testing of MS150-IR IoT-NTN Chipset on Iridium NTN Direct Satellite Network
gist: Mlink started live on-air testing of its MS150-IR NB-IoT chipset on Iridium's 3GPP-standard NTN Direct LEO network, moving from laboratory to orbital validation; certification and commercial availability are targeted before end-2026. The chipset is intended for automotive telematics, asset tracking and logistics applications requiring global satellite IoT connectivity.

headline: Toyota RAV4 Debuts Arene Vehicle OS in First Production SDV for Japanese Market
gist: Toyota's new-generation RAV4, launched in late 2025 and entering market in 2026, became the first production vehicle running Toyota's Arene vehicle OS platform, marking the start of Japan's SDV era. The integrated ECU architecture enables OTA software updates and continuous feature expansion, with further SDV models planned from 2026 onward.

headline: Waymo Recalls ~3,800 Autonomous Ride-Hailing Vehicles Over Software Defect in Flooded-Road Detection
gist: NHTSA reported in May 2026 that Waymo recalled 3,791 vehicles equipped with 5th- and 6th-generation ADS after a driverless vehicle failed to stop on a flooded high-speed road, with regulators estimating a 100% defect rate across the covered population. All affected vehicles received an interim OTA software fix by 20 April 2026, illustrating the role of OTA remediation in AV quality management.

headline: Kigen Automotive eSIM Becomes Industry's First GSMA eSA-Certified to SGP.32 v1.3 for Connected-Vehicle OEMs
gist: Arm's Kigen unit achieved GSMA eUICC Security Assurance (eSA) certification for its new Automotive eSIM built on Infineon's TEGRION SLI22 controller, the first ever certified to SGP.32 v1.3 with emergency-profile and post-quantum-era threat mitigations. OEM sampling in ETSI MFF2 package begins October 2026, with GSMA interoperability testing planned for the same month.
outlet: Media OutReach Newswire / Laotian Times (Kigen press release relay)

headline: CATL Starts Trial Cell Production on First Two Lines at 100 GWh Debrecen Plant
gist: CATL launched trial production on 22 September 2026 at its Debrecen, Hungary battery cell factory after securing all required permits and an occupancy certificate in August 2026, marking the transition from construction to line commissioning and process validation. The 100 GWh facility — CATL's largest outside China — targets NMC and LFP cells for European automakers; commercial mass-production timing was not disclosed.

headline: LG Energy Solution and B2U Storage Solutions Form U.S. Partnership to Repurpose EV Batteries for Grid-Scale BESS
gist: LG Energy Solution and B2U Storage Solutions announced a U.S. partnership under which B2U gains priority access to LG battery capacity to build cost-competitive grid-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) projects using repurposed EV cells. The deal addresses second-life battery economics and IRA-eligible domestic-content positioning.

headline: Rock Tech Lithium and Siemens Canada Sign Digital Twin and Engineering Agreements for Ontario Lithium Converter
gist: Rock Tech Lithium and Siemens Canada signed definitive agreements covering digital twin development and full engineering support for the planned Red Rock lithium hydroxide converter in Ontario. The definitive feasibility study is due by mid-December 2026, with the digital twin intended to optimize plant design and operations.

headline: LG Energy Solution BESS Earns NVIDIA DSX Ready Qualification for Data Centre Power Infrastructure
gist: LG Energy Solution's battery energy storage system qualified under the NVIDIA DSX Ready programme, certifying it for direct use in data centre power infrastructure alongside AI compute platforms. The qualification positions LGES BESS as a validated grid-edge storage solution within NVIDIA's data centre ecosystem.

headline: 8th V2G Business, Policy & Technology Forum Announced for Detroit, Featuring End-to-End Interoperability Demonstration
gist: Smart Grid Observer announced the 8th V2G Business, Policy & Technology Forum, scheduled for 27–29 October 2026 at the American Center for Mobility in Detroit, to feature an end-to-end V2G interoperability demonstration. The forum will focus on moving V2G from individual pilots toward scalable, interoperable commercial deployment.

headline: Volkswagen and Elli Prepare Q4 2026 Market Launch of Integrated Vehicle-to-Grid Offer for German Customers
gist: Volkswagen and its energy subsidiary Elli confirmed a Q4 2026 market launch for a fully integrated V2G product package in Germany, bundling the EV, a bidirectional charger, smart meter, app and electricity tariff in a single offer. The package enables private customers to feed stored power back to the grid and generate revenue, with pre-registration open since June 2026 and further European markets to follow.

headline: Soracom Launches Automotive Suite API Platform for Connected-Vehicle Lifecycle Connectivity Management
gist: Soracom launched Automotive Suite, an API-driven platform combining SGP.32 eSIM profile switching, multi-carrier management, in-car Wi-Fi and usage-based billing for managing connected-vehicle connectivity across the full vehicle lifecycle. The platform includes support for European emergency-call (eCall) services, directly targeting automotive OEMs and fleet operators.

headline: GM Adds ChargePoint Network to Energy Pass EV Charging Service
gist: GM expanded its Energy Pass charging service by adding ChargePoint's network, giving EV drivers access to ChargePoint DC fast and Level 2 stations through GM's in-vehicle and mobile apps. The companies also reported hundreds of new charging locations across the US, including NACS and CCS1 sites.

headline: CSA Group Issues Revised Public Notice of Intent for Standard Evaluating Cybersecurity of EV Charging Infrastructure
gist: CSA Group reissued a notice of intent for its standard defining a cybersecurity assessment framework for all EV charging equipment — residential Level 1/2, DC fast chargers and V2G units — covering security across design, procurement, operation and decommissioning. A second public comment period ran through June 30 2026, signalling imminent progression toward publication.

headline: Toyota Recalls 8,521 2026 C-HR EVs Over BEV ECU Software Bug Causing Battery Overcharge and Drive Shutdown
gist: Toyota filed NHTSA recall 26V570000 covering 8,521 model-year 2026 C-HR electric vehicles built February–July 2026, after engineers found a software flaw in the Denso-supplied BEV ECU that can allow regenerative braking to overcharge the traction battery and trigger a full electric drive shutdown. The remedy is a dealer-applied software update; owner notification letters were expected from mid-October 2026.

headline: IEA Publishes Dedicated Vehicle-to-Grid Technology Report Finding V2G Could Prevent 75% of Transformer Overloads by 2050
gist: The IEA released its first standalone V2G technology report, concluding that bidirectional EV charging could prevent three-quarters of electrical transformer overloads by 2050 compared with uncontrolled charging, based on modelling of San Francisco's distribution network. The report also flags inconsistent standards as the primary commercial barrier to scaling V2G globally.

headline: Sunwoda EVB Unveils 15C Ultra-Fast Charging Cell System That Charges 10%–97% in Nine Minutes
gist: Sunwoda EVB announced a 15C-rate battery cell system capable of charging from 10% to 97% state-of-charge in just nine minutes, representing a significant step toward ultra-fast charging that rivals petrol refuelling times. The system targets fleet and commercial EV operators and will require high-power charging infrastructure to realise its full charge rate.

headline: Fleet Data Silos Found to Hinder AI and Telematics Integration Across Mixed EV/ICE Fleets
gist: Industry surveys cited by FleetOwner and trade coverage show persistently low levels of full AI and telematics platform integration in mixed EV/ICE fleets, with fragmented maintenance and operational data identified as the primary bottleneck. Vendors including Geotab are developing unified workflow tools, natural-language query interfaces and edge-processing modules to address the gap.

headline: California Awards $1.1 Million to Develop World's First Curbside V2G EV Charger
gist: California awarded $1.1 million to Brooklyn-based EV charging company It's Electric to develop the world's first curbside vehicle-to-grid (V2G) charger, combining public on-street charging with grid export capability. The project is intended to demonstrate how urban kerb infrastructure can serve as a distributed grid resource without dedicated off-street real estate.

headline: NHTSA Announces 'Recalls Next' Public Meeting on OTA Updates and Technological Innovations in Safety Recalls
gist: NHTSA published a Federal Register notice in late September 2026 announcing a public meeting titled 'Recalls Next: Technological Innovations and Safety Recalls,' focusing on how connected-vehicle technologies, OTA software updates, and mobile repair are reshaping recall remediation. The notice explicitly calls out OTA as a tool to reduce time and burden of recall completion, with direct implications for off-highway OEMs adopting connected architectures.

headline: AEM Releases Whitepaper: 'From Assistance to Autonomy – How AI Is Changing Agricultural Equipment'
gist: AEM published a whitepaper on 10 September 2026 outlining three levels of AI integration in agricultural equipment — assist, automated, and autonomous — as a foundational framework for OEM product strategy and regulatory positioning. The paper addresses how AI-enabled equipment supports farm productivity, efficiency, and decision-making, and implicitly frames the policy landscape OEMs must navigate.

headline: Komatsu and EARTHBRAIN Enter Strategic Autonomy Partnership with AIM Intelligent Machines for Dozers and Excavators
gist: Komatsu and subsidiary EARTHBRAIN announced a strategic partnership with AIM Intelligent Machines to deliver autonomous construction solutions for bulldozers and hydraulic excavators in the U.S. and Japan, integrating AIM's physical AI platform with Komatsu's Smart Construction digital management system. Commercial deployment in the U.S. is already underway, with the Japanese market rollout planned for 2027.

headline: NMFTA Reveals Bendix EC80 Heavy-Truck Brake Controller Safety Recall Silently Patched Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
gist: Researchers from the National Motor Freight Traffic Association disclosed at Black Hat USA 2026 that a 2024 safety recall for Bendix's EC80 brake controller also remediated serious cybersecurity vulnerabilities — including a wirelessly reachable remote code execution flaw and a hardcoded password that could disable traction control — without public disclosure of the security fixes. The findings raise systemic questions about transparency in combined safety/security recalls for heavy off-highway and commercial vehicles.

headline: ASI Shifts Strategy to Off-Road Markets After Divesting Mining Unit to Epiroc, Redirects Automotive Team to Agriculture and Construction
gist: ASI announced it is redirecting its automotive proving-ground automation team to support agriculture, construction, landscaping, and logistics sectors following the divestiture of ASI Mining to Epiroc, which had held a 34% stake since 2018. Capital from the sale is enabling expanded customer deployments of ASI's Mobius OEM-agnostic fleet management and autonomy system.

headline: EU Cyber Resilience Act Compliance Obligations Crystallise for Off-Highway and AMHE OEMs with Digital Elements
gist: Analysis published in May 2026 confirms the EU Cyber Resilience Act applies to all 'Products with Digital Elements' placed on the EU market — explicitly including industrial automation and off-highway equipment control systems — mandating secure-by-default engineering, lifecycle vulnerability management, and CE marking alignment. Non-compliance carries tiered penalties of up to €15 million or 2.5% of global revenue, reshaping OEM product security obligations across agriculture, construction, and mining sectors.

headline: Deere FTC Settlement Implications Explored Alongside AGCO and CNH Precision Technology Leadership Shifts
gist: Farm Equipment's On the Record podcast examined the implications of John Deere's FTC settlement for the broader agricultural equipment industry, alongside leadership restructuring at AGCO and CNH in their precision agriculture and technology divisions. The episode signals mounting regulatory scrutiny of OEM data platform lock-in and repair-data access, with repercussions for telematics and data-management business models.

headline: Kubota Autonomous Robot Tractor Advances to Level 2+ with Remote Monitoring; KSAS SaaS Platform Surpasses 100,000 Accounts
gist: Japanese market analysis for 2026 confirms Kubota's AgriRobo tractor has reached Level 2 autonomy with LiDAR obstacle detection and remote monitoring, while its KSAS farm management SaaS platform has exceeded 100,000 accounts and is entering full monetisation. The 2026 models feature RTK precision improvements enabling centimetre-level accuracy, enabling one-operator-two-machine cooperative field operations.

headline: AEM Calls on Industry to 'Close the Connectivity Gap' for Non-Road Equipment OEMs
gist: AEM's newsroom flagged a prominent media coverage item headlined 'NOW IS THE TIME TO CLOSE THE CONNECTIVITY GAP,' reflecting the association's push for off-highway OEMs to accelerate embedded telematics and connectivity investment. The call aligns with AEM's 2026 trend analysis identifying mixed-fleet data interoperability (AEMP 2.0), satellite coverage, and regulations mandating OEM-installed telematics as key market drivers.

headline: Komatsu's Remote-Controlled Hydraulic Excavator with Contact-Prevention AI Demonstrated at Makuhari Messe
gist: Komatsu exhibited its remote-controlled hydraulic excavator featuring AI-powered cable and pipe contact-prevention at Makuhari Messe in June 2026, showcasing integration of real-time sensor data and remote operation via its EARTHBRAIN Smart Construction platform. The demonstration builds toward the commercial autonomy roadmap formalised in the AIM Intelligent Machines partnership.

headline: Berg Insight: SGP.32 eSIM Standard and Satellite Integration Drive Next Wave of OEM Connected-Vehicle Expansion to 583 Million Units
gist: Berg Insight analysis published in July 2026 projects the OEM connected-vehicle base at 583.1 million units, with expansion leaning heavily on the GSMA SGP.32 eSIM standard, 5G RedCap migration, and satellite integration for vehicles beyond cellular coverage — trends directly applicable to off-highway equipment operating in remote mining and agricultural environments. G+D, Rivian, and AT&T were cited as early adopters of SGP.32-compliant eSIM for remote network profile switching.

headline: UNECE R155 Scope Expected to Expand to Agricultural Vehicles; CRA vs. R155 Tension Remains Unresolved for Non-Road Machinery
gist: Regulatory analysis in 2026 confirms R156 already covers agricultural and forestry vehicles and trailers, while R155's extension to agricultural categories (T and R&S) remains under active discussion in WP.29 GRVA — creating dual compliance uncertainty alongside the EU Cyber Resilience Act. CEMA has flagged that CRA's supplier-side responsibility model differs fundamentally from R155's manufacturer-centric CSMS framework, posing challenges for SME component suppliers.

headline: Mordor Intelligence: Regulations Mandating OEM-Installed Telematics on Heavy Equipment Add 2.8% CAGR to Off-Highway Telematics Market
gist: Mordor Intelligence's 2026–2031 off-highway vehicle telematics market report identifies regulatory mandates for OEM-installed telematics as the top growth driver (+2.8% CAGR impact), followed by LEO satellite constellation deployment for black-spot-free coverage (+2.1%). The report highlights John Deere's Starlink integration and AEMP 2.0 mixed-fleet data-standard adoption as key competitive differentiators shaping the commercial model.

headline: Forbes: Physical AI and Autonomy-of-Things Retrofit Stacks Address Blue-Collar Labor Shortage in Construction, Agriculture and Mining
gist: A Forbes analysis published 18 September 2026 argues that OEM-agnostic physical AI retrofit platforms — exemplified by ASI's Mobius system — are gaining traction across construction, agriculture, and mining as mixed-fleet operators seek autonomy without full equipment replacement cycles. The article frames workforce shortage as the primary demand driver and notes growing investor appetite for aftermarket autonomy solutions that complement, rather than replace, incumbent OEM systems.

headline: Digital Twin Systems for Mine Safety: PMC/NIOSH Review Finds Real-Time Asset Models Enable Predictive Hazard Mitigation for Heavy Equipment
gist: A peer-reviewed article published in PMC in 2026 exploring digital twin systems in mine safety finds that continuously sensor-synced virtual replicas of heavy mining equipment can identify hazardous conditions in real time and trigger automated control responses, supporting both predictive maintenance and worker proximity safety. The review calls for broader adoption of digital twin frameworks across robotic and autonomous mining fleets as a functional safety complement to ISO 26262-derived approaches.
